title: Raksha Mantri chairs meeting of Consultative Committee of Ministry of Defence on ‘Modernisation of Indian Defence Forces’ in Jaisalmer
subtitle:
Govt is committed to building a technologically empowered military equipped to meet present-day & emerging challenges: Shri Rajnath Singh

“We aim to achieve Rs 3 lakh crore defence production & Rs 50,000 crore defence exports by 2029”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 NOV 2026 1:08PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh chaired the meeting of the Consultative Committee of the Ministry of Defence on ‘Modernisation of Indian Defence Forces’ in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan on November 3, 2026. The meeting witnessed comprehensive deliberations on the emerging security challenges, warfare paradigms, technological advancements and the imperative of building a future-ready, technologically empowered and operationally agile military. The key focus areas emerging from the meeting include:
Capability Development & Force Modernisation: Accelerating the induction of next-generation platforms, weapon systems and technologies to enhance combat effectiveness and operational preparedness.
Jointness & Integration: Strengthening Tri-service integration, joint operational planning and synergised application of capabilities across multiple domains.
Indigenous Defence Manufacturing: Giving further impetus to Make-in-India and Aatmanirbhar Bharat through indigenous research, design, development and manufacturing, with greater participation of domestic industry, start-ups and academia.
Emerging & Disruptive Technologies: Harnessing artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, unmanned platforms, cyber, space, electronic warfare and advanced communications to prepare for the character of future conflicts.
Defence Research & Innovation: Strengthening collaboration among the Defence Forces, DRDO, Defence Public Sector Undertakings, private industry and academic institutions to accelerate the transition from innovation to operational capability.
Resource Optimisation & Implementation: Establishing clear priorities, institutional mechanisms and measurable milestones to ensure that modernisation initiatives translate into tangible operational outcomes.
Emphasising the need for the Defence Forces to remain prepared for present-day and emerging challenges, Raksha Mantri enumerated the steps taken by the Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, across three key dimensions - ‘Budget & Capital Acquisition and Self-reliance’, ‘Technology’ and ‘Human Capital’ - to equip the military to meet the evolving demands of technology-driven modern warfare. He highlighted the Government's sustained focus on budgetary support and capital acquisition to meet the modernisation requirements, stressing that adequate financial resources, coupled with effective utilisation and prioritisation of critical needs of the Services, are essential to strengthening military capabilities.
Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the defence budget for the Financial Year (FY) 2026-27 was increased to a record Rs 7.85 lakh crore, including a capital outlay of Rs 2.19 lakh crore earmarked for modernisation and capital procurement, reflecting the commitment to meeting the operational requirements of the Defence Forces while bolstering domestic defence industries and manufacturing capabilities.
On the growing Aatmanirbharta in defence, Raksha Mantri said that defence production has risen from Rs 46,429 crore in FY 2014-15 to a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in FY 2025-26, with defence exports, which stood at less than Rs 2,000 crore in 2014, growing to approximately Rs 40,000 crore. “We aim to achieve defence production worth Rs 3 lakh crore and defence exports worth Rs 50,000 crore by 2029,” he added.
Shri Rajnath Singh underlined the transformative role of technology in modern warfare, stating that technological advancements are integral to the changing character of conflicts. He highlighted the initiatives undertaken by DRDO in developing advanced weapons, missiles and systems, adding that the Government is providing a level playing field to the private sector, enabling greater participation of entities ranging from MSMEs to large corporations in the defence ecosystem. Describing it as a 'whole-of-the-nation' approach, he expressed satisfaction at the growing contribution of private industry towards strengthening the defence capabilities of the country.
Underscoring the importance of human capital, Raksha Mantri stated that the strength of a military is determined not merely by technology and financial resources, but also by the capabilities & preparedness of personnel. “The rapidly evolving nature of warfare necessitates that our Defence Forces remain aligned with the changing requirements of modern warfare. Keeping this in mind, all three Services have continuously refined their structures and formations. The Indian Army’s new formations, including the ‘Asani’, ‘Bhairav’ and ‘Shaktiban’ platoons, are proving highly effective in addressing contemporary operational requirements and adapting to the changing dynamics of the battlefield,” he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised that modernisation is not just about procuring new weapons and equipment, it entails enhancing the operational preparedness of the Defence Forces, equipping them with modern technologies and developing indigenous capabilities for the long term. Underlining the significance of ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ in the context of national security, he highlighted that the focus is to build a robust domestic defence ecosystem that aligns technological development with military requirements, encourages greater participation of Indian industry and reduces the country’s strategic dependence on foreign sources. Strategic autonomy and indigenous technological capabilities are essential to safeguarding national security, he said.
Raksha Mantri underscored that modernisation is a continuous process, necessitating sustained efforts to enhance operational preparedness in response to evolving technologies, shifting security challenges and changing requirements. He emphasised the need to build long-term capabilities that would enable the Defence Forces to remain operationally effective and self-reliant. He called for sustained promotion of research and development, indigenous technologies, greater industrial participation and innovation to strengthen the country's defence capabilities.
The meeting witnessed valuable suggestions by Members of Parliament from both the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha. Their diverse perspectives and insights enriched the consultative process, bringing in important legislative, strategic and national perspectives. The deliberations translated into a clear roadmap for action, with emphasis on prioritising critical capabilities, strengthening coordination among stakeholders, streamlining acquisition and development processes, and periodically assessing progress against defined objectives.
Emphasising the need to translate intent into implementation, the meeting highlighted the importance of a structured and phased approach to modernisation. The objective is to build a military capable of responding effectively to conventional, sub-conventional and multi-domain security challenges.
Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, Secretary (Ex-servicemen Welfare) Smt Sukriti Likhi, Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay and other senior civil & military officials attended the meeting.

The release was unveiled today at a press event in New Delhi, in the presence of Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), said, The development of such indigenous models strengthens India’s technological and strategic autonomy in Artificial Intelligence. It also opens up opportunities to improve productivity and efficiency across government, industry, research and education. These resources have supported the development of models such as EKA-1 and Dhīr, each addressing distinct and relevant use cases. Through platforms such as AIKosh, these models can be made accessible to researchers, students, innovators and the wider public, encouraging further experimentation and innovation.
Speaking on the advancement of indigenous AI capabilities, Shri Sudeep Shrivastava, COO, IndiaAI, said, "IndiaAI Mission's comprehensive support ecosystem is dedicated to making artificial intelligence more accessible and tailored to India's unique landscape. Breakthrough models like Dhīr and EKA-1 showcase the nation's multi-layered progress in AI ranging from lightweight solutions optimized for everyday devices to robust powerhouses engineered for complex enterprise applications."
Soket AI and ZenteiQ are among the teams selected under the IndiaAI Innovation Centre (Foundation Models) pillar of the IndiaAI Mission to build indigenous foundation AI capabilities and Large Language Models. Access to subsidized national AI compute infrastructure and support for ancillary research expenses under the mission enabled the development of these models, highlighting how public AI infrastructure can accelerate homegrown innovation.

Soket Labs Technology and Research Private Limited has developed
EKA-1
, a powerful Foundation Model featuring 26.3 billion parameters and trained on approximately 7.5 trillion tokens.
EKA-1 demonstrates advanced capabilities, spanning all 22 scheduled Indian languages alongside English. Built as an open, sparse hybrid language model, EKA-1 is designed for math, code, reasoning, and agentic use.
Speaking at the release, Abhishek Upperwal, CEO, Soket Labs Technology and Research Private Limited, said,  “With the support of the IndiaAI Mission, we have developed an advanced AI model specifically tailored to India's unique banking, financial services and cybersecurity landscape. Dhīr 2B
and
Dhīr 5B
open-source models. These models can be deployed as secure, on-premise, multilingual assistants supporting English and 10 Indian languages.

Speaking at the release, Prof. Sashikumar, CEO, ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations, said, “Models like Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B offer the flexibility to run across different computing platforms, including GPUs and TPUs. This allows users to access AI capabilities locally while keeping data on their devices, enhancing privacy, security and accessibility.”

title: India to pursue Solution-oriented and Equitable Climate Action at UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya: Union Environment Minister
subtitle: Predictable Climate Finance, Party-Driven Mitigation and Adaptation Outcomes, Technology Transfer and Just Transition to be India's Focus: Shri Bhupender Yadav
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 NOV 2026 2:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, outlined India’s priorities for COP31 of the UNFCCC, to be held in Antalya, Türkiye, from 9th to 20th November 2026, and highlighted the key outcomes of India’s participation in CBD COP17 and UNCCD COP17. Briefing the media in New Delhi today the Minister said India will approach COP31 with a solution-oriented vision, bringing practical solutions for the Global South, with capacity building, knowledge sharing and geography-specific solutions at the core. India will work closely with G-77 and China, LMDC and BASIC, he informed.
The Minister reaffirmed that India stands committed to make positive contributions to global efforts to achieve objectives of climate convention and goals of Paris Agreement. He said Climate finance will be a key priority, with India seeking a COP31 decision to commence the Climate Finance Work Programme. Shri Yadav emphasised that finance is an obligation of developed countries under Article 9.1 and must be predictable, largely public and concessional, and should not add to the debt burden. India will also press for mitigation and the Global Stocktake to remain Party-driven, facilitative and non-punitive, respecting the nationally determined nature of NDCs and ruling out new top-down targets.
Further, the Minister informed that
Adaptation will remain a priority for India, with Global Goal on Adaptation indicators being voluntary and not conditioning access to finance, alongside scaled-up adaptation finance. India will support continuation of the Just Transition Work Programme through a Party-driven mechanism, viewing just transition through the lens of climate justice, the right to development and affordable energy access. On technology, India will emphasise that technology transfer is an obligation of developed countries and that barriers related to cost, IPR and trade must be addressed. Participation in carbon markets should remain voluntary. India will also underline that voluntary initiatives under the Presidency Action Agenda should remain separate from negotiations and that uniform global targets must respect national circumstances.
India will also highlight the linkage between the need for adaptation in agriculture, food security
and the livelihoods of small and marginal farmers. Its engagements at COP31 will include LeadIT 3.0 with Sweden, in addition to high-level side events on coastal resilience, panels on IBCA and forests. Shri Yadav said India will play a constructive, bridge-building role in Antalya, seeking an outcome that moves from commitments to implementation and support.
Shri Yadav informed that during
CBD COP17 in Yerevan (Armenia)
, India's reaffirmed its commitment to the effective and equitable implementation of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF), underscoring the importance of national priorities, circumstances and legislative frameworks, community participation, fair and equitable benefit-sharing, and adequate and predictable financial resources, capacity-building and technology transfer. During the negotiations, he stated, India strongly advocated the fulfilment of developed countries' obligations under Article 20(2) of the Convention, opposed any mandatory expansion of the contributor base or shifting of existing financial responsibilities onto developing countries, and called for accessible, adequate and equitable biodiversity finance. On Digital Sequence Information (DSI), Shri Yadav highlighted that India emphasised the need for fair and equitable benefit-sharing through the multilateral mechanism, including the Cali Fund, while underscoring the importance of respecting national access and benefit-sharing (ABS) frameworks and sovereign rights. India also advocated a party-driven, facilitative, non-intrusive and non-punitive approach to the global review of KMGBF implementation, guided by national circumstances and priorities, and emphasised the need for a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach to biodiversity conservation and implementation, he added.
Talking about
UNCCD COP17 in Ulaanbaatar (Mongolia)
, the Minister stated that India highlighted land restoration as central to food and water security, biodiversity, livelihoods and rural economies. He informed that India, after being elected Chair of the Asia-Pacific Regional Group, reiterated its commitment to restore over 26 million hectares by 2030 and called for diversified, adequate, predictable and sustained international finance for restoration and drought resilience. Shri Yadav highlighted that India advocated a shift from drought response to drought resilience, supported science-based and community-led restoration of rangelands, and highlighted pastoralists as custodians and partners. India also launched its first
Guide to Grasslands and Other Open Natural Ecosystems of India
, underscoring its science-based, landscape-specific approach to restoration, the Minister stated.
Shri Yadav said India’s engagement across the three processes reflects its commitment to equity, national circumstances, science-based solutions and adequate means of implementation, particularly for developing countries. At COP31, India will work towards balanced and practical outcomes that strengthen implementation, support and international cooperation. Other dignitaries present on the occasion included Secretary (MoEFCC), Shri Narendra Bhooshan; Additional Secretaries, Dr. Amandeep Garg and Shri Ashutosh Agnihotri; Joint Secretaries, Shri Rajat Agarwal and Shri Uday Chaudhari; IG (Forest), Dr. Clement Ben, besides other senior officers of the Ministry.

Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Alias Lalan Singh), Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India, participated in a programme organised by the Sikkim Milk Union (SMU) at Gangtok, Sikkim, on 3 November 2026. The programme focused on strengthening dairy infrastructure, expanding cooperative networks and promoting value addition in the dairy sector.
The Hon’ble Union Minister inaugurated the Microbiology Laboratory of the Sikkim Milk Union under the National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD). The facility was aimed at strengthening microbiological testing and quality assessment, thereby contributing to improved quality assurance and food safety in the dairy sector. He also inspected the exhibition stalls showcasing dairy products and other initiatives of the Sikkim Milk Union.
The programme commenced with a welcome address by the Chairman of the Sikkim Milk Union, followed by the felicitation of the Hon’ble Union Minister and other dignitaries. The Microbiology Laboratory at Karfectar was also virtually inaugurated. The Churpi Traceability initiative was inaugurated to strengthen traceability and promote the identity and marketability of the traditional dairy product. The Hon’ble Union Minister also witnessed the launch of Fodder Plus products developed by Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), highlighting the importance of fodder availability, farmer collectives and diversified income opportunities in the livestock sector.
Registration certificates were distributed to five newly established Dairy Cooperative Societies (DCSs), marking another step towards strengthening the cooperative dairy network in Sikkim and expanding the reach of organised dairy institutions at the grassroots level.
Sikkim recorded 79% growth in milk production over the last decade
Addressing the gathering, the Hon’ble Union Minister congratulated the Government of Sikkim and stakeholders on the significant progress made in the dairy sector. He highlighted that milk production had increased by 79%, from 1.37 lakh litres to 2.45 lakh litres per day, while the number of dairy cooperative societies had grown by 88%, from 389 in 2014–15 to 733 in 2025–26. Daily milk supply to consumers had also doubled from 28,000 litres to 56,000 litres.
Emphasising the need to accelerate dairy development, he called upon NDDB to intensify its efforts and deploy additional human resources to help Sikkim achieve self-reliance in milk production and procurement. He underlined the role of dairy cooperatives in ensuring milk quality, preventing adulteration and securing fair returns for farmers.
Citing the example of Varanasi, he highlighted how NDDB's intervention had increased milk collection from 14,000 litres per day in 2022 to approximately 2.5 lakh litres per day. The price received by farmers had also increased from ₹28–30 to ₹42 per litre, with additional income opportunities through cow dung utilisation in biogas plants under the GOBARdhan initiative
.
Centre of Excellence for indigenous Siri cattle
Referring to his visit to Mangan, where local cattle yielded an average of approximately three litres of milk per day, the Hon’ble Minister announced that the Central Government would sanction funds for establishing a Centre of Excellence for the conservation and development of indigenous Siri cattle. The proposed centre would promote advanced breeding technologies, including IVF, to improve the genetic potential and milk productivity of the breed. He invited the State Government to submit a formal proposal for consideration.
Modernisation of Mangan dairy plant
The Hon’ble Minister further stated that NDDB would finance and undertake the comprehensive modernisation of the existing dairy processing plant in Mangan district, following the successful model implemented in Mizoram.
Concluding his address, he reiterated the Central Government’s commitment to Sikkim's dairy and agricultural development, stating that the State's economic progress was integral to strengthening the North Eastern region and advancing the Prime Minister’s vision of an Aatmanirbhar North East.

title: NLMC Organises Pre-Bid Meeting for E-Auction of 5.119-Acre HIL (India) Limited Land Parcel in New Delhi
subtitle:
Third e-auction publicly advertised by NLMC in the last two months reflects the Government's continued thrust on monetisation of surplus public sector land assets

Strategically located land parcel on Rohtak Road carries a reserve price of ₹829.69 crore and offers development potential of FSI 400 under applicable TOD provisions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 NOV 2026 5:11PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC), under the administrative control of the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Ministry of Finance, Government of India, organised a Pre-Bid Meeting in New Delhi today, in connection with the proposed e-auction of a strategically located land parcel owned by HIL (India) Limited.
The meeting was organised to familiarise prospective bidders with the property's location, key features, development potential, applicable land-use provisions, eligibility requirements and the terms and conditions governing the e-auction. Representatives from NLMC, HIL (India) Limited and CBRE India, the transaction advisor, participated in the meeting and provided detailed information to prospective bidders regarding the property and the bidding process.
The Pre-Bid Meeting provided a platform for prospective participants to interact with the concerned officials, seek clarifications on the Request for Proposal (RFP), understand the technical and financial bid submission requirements and obtain information necessary for informed participation in the e-auction.
Third E-Auction by NLMC in Two Months: Advancing the Government's Land Monetisation Agenda
The proposed monetisation of the HIL (India) Limited land parcel marks the third e-auction publicly advertised by NLMC in the last two months. This reflects the sustained efforts being undertaken by the Government of India to accelerate the monetisation of surplus and underutilised land and other non-core assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs).
Through these successive e-auctions, NLMC is facilitating the identification, structuring and monetisation of public-sector land assets, with the objective of unlocking their economic value and enabling their productive utilisation through transparent and competitive processes.
The initiative is aligned with the Government's broader asset monetisation programme, which seeks to unlock the value of existing public assets, encourage private-sector participation and facilitate the generation of resources for further economic development.
Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Rohan Chand Thakur (IAS), Chief Executive Officer, National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC), said,
"The Government of India has accorded significant priority to the monetisation of surplus and underutilised land assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises. The third e-auction publicly advertised by NLMC within the last two months reflects our continued efforts to translate this priority into tangible outcomes. Our endeavour is to unlock the economic value of public assets through transparent, structured and competitive processes while facilitating their productive utilisation. The HIL land parcel, given its strategic location and development potential, presents an opportunity for eligible participants to explore its future utilisation. The Pre-Bid Meeting is an important step towards ensuring clarity, transparency and informed participation in the bidding process."
Mr. Kuldeep Singh, Chairman and Managing Director, HIL (India) Limited, stated,
"The land parcel being offered for outright sale is strategically located on Rohtak Road, Shivaji Marg, New Delhi, and represents a significant asset of HIL (India). Spread over approximately 5.119 acres, the property offers substantial development potential, with an FSI of 400 along with the applicable FSI based on TOD provisions, subject to the prescribed statutory conditions and approvals. Through this monetisation initiative, we seek to facilitate the productive utilisation of the asset while providing prospective developers and eligible bidders an opportunity to participate in its future development. We encourage interested participants to examine the auction documents and actively participate in the competitive bidding process."
Strategic Location and Development Potential
The land parcel being offered for outright sale measures approximately
5.119 acres
and is situated in the Najafgarh Industrial Area, along Rohtak Road, Shivaji Marg, New Delhi. The property enjoys a prominent location with approximately
140 metres of frontage along Rohtak Road
, offering visibility and connectivity to key parts of the National Capital.
The site also benefits from connectivity through the Delhi Metro's Green Line, providing convenient public transport access. Its location, accessibility and surrounding urban infrastructure make it a significant property with potential for suitable redevelopment and future utilisation, subject to applicable regulations and statutory approvals.
The property has an indicated development potential of FSI up to 400 along with the applicable FSI based on TOD provisions, subject to the applicable provisions of the Master Plan for Delhi 2021, relevant redevelopment policies, statutory requirements and approvals from the competent authorities. The reserve price for the land parcel has been fixed at ₹829.69 crore.
Key Features and Auction Parameters
During the meeting, prospective bidders were apprised of the important features and participation conditions of the proposed e-auction, including:
Property Area:
Approximately 5.119 acres.
Location:
Najafgarh Industrial Area, Rohtak Road, Shivaji Marg, New Delhi.
Road Frontage:
Approximately 140 metres along Rohtak Road.
Development Potential:
FSI of 400 under applicable TOD provisions, subject to statutory conditions and approvals.
Reserve Price:
₹829.69 crore.
Mode of Sale:
Outright sale through an online e-auction.
Bidding Parameter:
Highest auction price, with bidding in multiples of ₹1 crore per acre.
Consortium Participation:
Permitted, with a maximum of three members.
EMD Payment:
Through Bank Guarantee or NEFT/RTGS, as stipulated in the RFP.
Land Use:
Industrial use, with conversion permissible subject to applicable norms and approvals.
Applicable Policy:
Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Policy, as applicable.
The participants were also briefed on the process for registration, submission of technical bids, compliance with eligibility criteria, payment of the Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) and participation in the online auction. The meeting provided an opportunity to clarify procedural and technical aspects of the transaction and familiarise prospective bidders with the prescribed bidding framework.
NLMC's Role in Advancing Public Asset Monetisation
The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC) is a wholly owned Government of India company functioning under the administrative control of the Department of Public Enterprises, Ministry of Finance. It has been established to undertake and facilitate the monetisation of surplus land and building assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises and other Government agencies.
NLMC works in coordination with concerned CPSEs and other stakeholders to identify surplus and underutilised assets, undertake the necessary transaction structuring and facilitate their monetisation through transparent and competitive mechanisms.
The ongoing series of e-auctions, including the proposed HIL (India) Limited land parcel sale, represents the continued operationalisation of the Government's asset monetisation agenda. content:
Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to mandate drug manufacturers to formally authorise a person with appropriate qualifications and experience for batch release of drugs and maintain prescribed records for every batch manufactured.
The proposed amendments aim to strengthen accountability in the drug manufacturing process by introducing an explicit regulatory requirement for the authorisation of personnel responsible for batch release. While manufacturing licences currently require manufacturers to furnish details of competent technical staff responsible for manufacturing and testing, there is no specific provision for mentioning the person authorised to undertake batch release.
Under the proposed framework, applicants seeking manufacturing licences under the relevant provisions of the Drugs Rules, 1945, would be required to designate a suitably qualified and experienced person for batch release and maintain batch-release records in accordance with the prescribed requirements. The amendments also propose to introduce a prescribed format for the Batch Release Certificate under the Rules.
Batch release is a critical stage in the pharmaceutical manufacturing process, involving an overall review of the relevant quality parameters and documentation before a batch is released for distribution. The proposed requirements are intended to establish clear responsibility for this function, ensure traceability of batch-release decisions and provide an additional level of oversight of product quality.
The proposed amendments are also expected to support manufacturers in strengthening their compliance with applicable Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and reinforce the regulatory framework governing the quality assurance of drugs.
Objections and suggestions, if any, on the proposed amendments may be submitted to the Under Secretary (Drugs Regulation), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, U-6, Work Hall, C Wing, First Floor, Kartavya Bhawan-1, New Delhi – 110001, or sent by email to

title: Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare proposes expansion of authorised Import gateways for Drugs, Medical Devices and Cosmetics
subtitle: Proposed amendment to Drugs Rules, 1945, seeks to add additional Inland Container Depots, Special Economic Zones and an international airport to facilitate efficient import and clearance of healthcare products
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:

content:
Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed an amendment to Rule 43A of the Drugs Rules, 1945, to expand the network of authorised entry points for the import of drugs, medical devices and cosmetics into the country. The proposed amendment aims to facilitate smoother import operations, improve logistics efficiency and strengthen the supply chain for healthcare products.
Rule 43A of the Drugs Rules, 1945, specifies the authorised ports, airports, railway stations, road crossings and other entry points through which drugs may be imported into India. With a view to facilitating trade and improving the efficiency of import-related processes, the Ministry has proposed the inclusion of additional Inland Container Depots (ICDs), a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) and an international airport in the list of authorised locations.
The proposed additional locations are ICD Sonipat, Piyala and Harsaru in Haryana; ICD Dadri in Uttar Pradesh; ICD Gandhidham/Mundra in Gujarat; ICD Sanath Nagar and Thimmapur in Hyderabad, Telangana; ICD Whitefield in Bengaluru, Karnataka; SEZ Bommasandra in Karnataka; and Noida International Airport in Uttar Pradesh for the import of drugs by air.
These locations will be added to the existing network of authorised import gateways, which includes ICDs at Dhannad and Tihi in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, along with the airports already notified for the import of drugs.
The proposed expansion is expected to facilitate importers in clearing consignments closer to their manufacturing facilities, warehouses and distribution centres. This is likely to reduce inland transportation distances, optimise logistics costs and minimise delays in the movement of imported consignments. The measure is also expected to improve operational convenience for importers while facilitating more efficient movement of medicines, medical devices and cosmetics across different regions of the country.
Through this proposed amendment, the Ministry seeks to strengthen the supporting infrastructure for the import of healthcare products, promote ease of doing business and contribute towards a more efficient and responsive supply chain, thereby facilitating timely availability of essential healthcare products.

He said that the appeal to armed Naxalites to surrender had yielded positive results: only 10 per cent of the Naxalites were killed, while 90 per cent surrendered. Jantana Sarkar

title: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) and Government of Bihar Sign MoU for Scientific Desilting of Water Bodies and Utilisation of Silt in National Highway Projects
subtitle:
Scientific desilting to enhance water-carrying capacity, improve drainage and reduce flood risks

‘Nadi Sanjivani’ initiative to integrate river restoration, flood management and agricultural conservation with highway infrastructure development

243 lakh cubic metres of silt to be utilised in 16 ongoing National Highway projects; 835 lakh cubic metres proposed for 27 future projects
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 NOV 2026 4:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant step towards integrating water-body restoration with infrastructure development, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) and the Government of Bihar today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for scientific desilting of identified rivers and other water bodies and utilisation of suitable excavated silt in National Highway construction projects in Bihar. The MoU was signed in New Delhi in the presence of Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Shri Nitin Gadkari and Bihar Chief Minister Shri Samrat Choudhary.
Envisioned as
‘Nadi Sanjivani’
, the initiative seeks to restore the water-carrying capacity of rivers and water bodies, strengthen flood management, conserve agricultural land and provide a sustainable source of construction material for National Highway projects. It presents an integrated approach to addressing water-management challenges while supporting infrastructure expansion.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Nitin Gadkari highlighted that accumulated silt has significantly affected the carrying capacity of rivers, contributing to floods, damage to agricultural land and loss of property. Bihar faces recurring challenges of flooding and water scarcity, particularly due to rivers originating in Nepal that carry substantial quantities of water and sediment into the State. He emphasised that scientific desilting would help improve water flow and drainage, restore water bodies and make suitable excavated material available for highway construction.
The Union Minister stated that the initiative would create a mutually beneficial framework in which river restoration supports infrastructure development, while utilisation of excavated silt reduces dependence on fresh earth material and agricultural soil. This would help conserve productive agricultural land, reduce construction costs and facilitate faster completion of highway projects. He further emphasised that implementation would be undertaken in coordination with the Bihar Government with appropriate technical assessments and safeguards. Expressing confidence in the initiative, Shri Gadkari said that the model could be extended to other States facing similar challenges, promoting sustainable infrastructure development and improved water management.
Shri Samrat Choudhary, Chief Minister of Bihar, highlighted the State’s longstanding vulnerability to recurring floods, which cause substantial losses to farmers, agricultural land, livelihoods and infrastructure. He underscored the need for scientific management of rivers and water bodies to address the adverse impact of accumulated silt on their water-carrying capacity.
The Chief Minister informed that the
Bihar Water Sources Restoration and Silt Management Policy, 2026
, has been formulated to provide a structured framework for restoration of water bodies and management of accumulated silt. The policy also facilitates removal of sand and silt deposited on agricultural land following floods, providing relief to affected farmers.
Welcoming the MoU, Shri Choudhary said that the initiative would strengthen Bihar’s efforts towards flood management, agricultural development and infrastructure expansion. He noted that restoration of water bodies would improve their carrying capacity, enhance water availability for irrigation and drinking purposes, support groundwater recharge and contribute to reducing flood-related risks. He assured full cooperation of the State Government in facilitating implementation and timely processing of proposals.
Significant potential for utilisation of silt in highway projects
NHAI has identified substantial potential for utilisation of excavated silt in National Highway projects in Bihar. Under the initiative,
243 lakh cubic metres of suitable silt will be utilised in 16 ongoing projects
, while an estimated
835 lakh cubic metres is proposed for utilisation in 27 future projects
, subject to technical suitability and requisite approvals.
Currently, 39 NHAI projects covering approximately 1,561 km, with an estimated investment of ₹58,340 crore, are under construction in Bihar. Another 11 projects covering around 1,982 km and involving an estimated investment of ₹1,85,200 crore are proposed.
The availability of suitable excavated silt is expected to meet a significant part of the material requirement of these projects, reduce construction costs and facilitate timely execution of highway works.
Scientific implementation with safeguards and monitoring
The MoU establishes an institutional framework for coordinated and time-bound implementation between NHAI and the Government of Bihar in accordance with the Bihar Water Sources Restoration and Silt Management Policy, 2026, and applicable environmental and statutory provisions.
The Road Construction Department (RCD), Government of Bihar, will act as the nodal department, supported by a State-level Coordination Committee to examine proposals, facilitate approvals, monitor implementation and resolve operational issues.
Desilting will be undertaken through scientific methods following detailed technical assessments of identified water bodies. Extraction will be permitted only at approved locations and within prescribed technical limits, ensuring that river ecosystems, riverbanks, embankments, bridges and other structures are not adversely affected.
The suitability of excavated silt for National Highway construction will be established through appropriate testing in accordance with applicable MoRTH specifications and relevant Indian Roads Congress (IRC) codes. Joint measurement, digital record-keeping, regular monitoring and periodic reconciliation of extracted, transported and utilised quantities will ensure transparency and accountability.
Expanding connectivity across Bihar
The Government of India has significantly expanded National Highway infrastructure in Bihar, with the network increasing from 4,615 km in 2014 to approximately 6,500 km at present. Since 2014, construction of around 29 new bridges over major rivers in Bihar has also been taken up to strengthen regional connectivity and facilitate movement of people and goods.
The MoU marks an important step towards integrating river restoration, flood management, agricultural conservation and infrastructure development through sustainable resource utilisation. By converting excavated silt into a productive construction resource, the initiative will help conserve agricultural land, improve efficiency in highway construction and support restoration of water bodies.
‘Nadi Sanjivani’ represents a sustainable development model in which river restoration and infrastructure creation complement each other, paving the way for a more resilient, better-connected and prosperous Bihar.
The occasion was attended by NHAI Chairman Shri Santosh Kumar Yadav, Director General Shri Sudeep Chaudhary, NHIDCL Managing Director Shri Krishna Kumar, Bihar Government Secretaries Shri Pankaj Pal and Shri Atul Kumar, and other senior officials and dignitaries.

title: VELC on board Aditya-L1 reveals asymmetric expansion of solar eruption that could impact space weather
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 NOV 2026 12:17PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India’s first space-based solar observatory, Aditya-L1 has helped scientists take a peek into the nature of expansion of a solar eruption or a coronal mass eruption (CME) and gain new insights into it. This could be important for space-weather studies and thereby affecting our satellites and communication networks.
Aditya L 1 satellite launched in September 2023 is now operational at the Sun–Earth L1 point, providing continuous observations of the Sun. It carries 7 payloads, of which the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC), the primary payload, is an internally occulted coronagraph designed to observe the solar corona simultaneously in various modes.
By combining data from the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph on Aditya-L1 with complementary observations from NASA’s SDO spacecraft and three-dimensional modeling, scientists from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), an autonomous institution of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) were able to reconstruct the full 3-D geometry and dynamics of solar eruptions.
Their study published in Astrophysical Journal Letters, showed, for the first time, that the CME did not expand outward from the Sun like a simple symmetric bubble, as previously thought. Instead, it underwent non-uniform expansion and developed an asymmetric shape. These differences in CME expansion can affect its speed as it travels towards Earth causing space-weather disturbances.
The VELC studies nascent CMEs through spectroscopy in the 530.3 nm wavelength green emission line due to highly ionized iron atoms in the corona. This line emission captures hot coronal plasma which is at temperatures of around 1.8 million Kelvin. The Doppler shift, or the change in the wavelength of this emission line provides information about plasma velocity along the line of sight, and close to the solar disk.
The VELC, with this unique capability, was designed and fabricated by the IIA at its MGK Menon Lab for Space Sciences on the CREST campus in
Hosakote, with substantial support from ISRO.
“We observed the CME that occurred on 5 August 2024 using the VELC as well as data from the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) onboard NASA’s Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO)”, explained Saurabh Tripathi, a PhD student at IIA, and lead author of the study. The CME was launched from an active region near the western limb of the Sun. VELC’s spectroscopic data show an unusual yet distinct Doppler pattern of blueward and red-ward shifted emission, which arises from plasma moving towards and away from us, respectively.
“Our results show that the CME did not expand uniformly. The AIA images captured how the CME propagated across the sky, while VELC revealed the motion of the expanding CME bubble towards and away from us,” Tanmoy Samanta, a solar astronomer at IIA and the corresponding author of the study elaborated. Together, these observations reveal that the CME did not expand like a simple spherical bubble. Instead, its uneven expansion caused it to develop an asymmetric shape.
“To understand the unusual spectral pattern observed by VELC, we then developed a 3-D geometric-kinematic model of an expanding CME”, said Jayant Joshi of IIA and a co-author. The model was used to test how the CME’s orientation and uneven sideways expansion could produce the spectral structures observed by VELC. A model with symmetric expansion could not reproduce the observed pattern. Instead, a model of an inclined CME axis and asymmetric lateral expansion produced a spectral pattern and temporal evolution similar to those observed by VELC. The researchers plan to use this technique on other CMEs, to reconstruct their motion without relying entirely on multi-viewpoint imaging from telescopes in space. This complementarity is particularly valuable in the lower corona, where CMEs evolve rapidly, and their motion along the line of sight cannot be obtained from imaging alone.
Fig
. (Left) Composite image of the Sun’s corona combining data from India's Aditya-L1/VELC (outer part, 1.05–1.5 solar radii) and NASA’s SDO/AIA (inner disk). (Top right) Aditya-L1/VELC spectra recorded during the eruption, showing two distinct branches of emission — one shifted toward shorter wavelengths (plasma moving toward us) and one toward longer wavelengths (plasma moving away) — the spectral signature of a three-dimensional, asymmetric solar eruption. (Bottom right) Model spectra reproducing the observed pattern, confirming asymmetric lateral expansion of the CME in the inner corona
“The asymmetric shape of an early CME can have important implications for how it interacts with the solar wind and experiences drag during its propagation through the heliosphere. Such effects can influence the CME’s speed and, ultimately, its arrival time at Earth”, said Joshi.

https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/aea295

title: Sarbananda Sonowal Outlines Plan to Double Coastal & Waterway Freight Share to 12% by 2047

Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme and Cruise Bharat Mission expected to create more than 560,000 jobs and save 16 million tons of carbon dioxide emissions

India's maritime sector is undergoing massive transformations: Sonowal at Consultative Committee meeting in Puri

content:
Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal, said at a Consultative Committee meeting in Puri, Odisha, that the government is working to double the share of coastal and inland waterway shipping in India's freight movement from 6% to 12% by 2047, and to attract 1 million sea cruise passengers by 2029, through two proposed initiatives: the Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme and the Cruise Bharat Mission.
The Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal also announced that Puri International Cruise Terminal will be developed by Paradip Port Authority (PPA) in partnership
with the Government
of Odisha. The project is likely to be developed at a cost of Rs 1,500 crores.
Sonowal chaired a meeting of the ministry's Consultative Committee on strengthening coastal and cruise shipping.
Minister of State of MoPSW Shantanu Thakur
and eight members of Parliament attended. The ministry's secretary introduced the topic by outlining measures to promote coastal and cruise shipping.
"In the last 12 years under PM Narendra Modi
,
India's maritime sector
has undergone
massive transformations,"
Sonowal
said.
India has more than 11,000 kilometers (6,800 miles) of coastline, a natural advantage for moving freight over long distances more cleanly. Coastal cargo at Indian ports has surged from 74 million metric tons to 177 million metric tons over the past 12 years, growth of about 140%, Sonowal said.
“Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi
’s
dynamic leadership, our coastline and our rivers are being turned into engines of growth. The Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme and the Cruise Bharat Mission will move more cargo by sea and bring more visitors to our shores, creating jobs and protecting the environment,”
Sarbananda Sonowal
said.
The Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme, announced in the 2026-27 budget, will offer incentives to cargo owners, coastal vessel operators and multimodal transport operators, who move cargo by more than one means of transport, such as ship, rail and road.
Sea cruises are also growing fast, Sonowal said. In the 2025-26 fiscal year, India recorded 462,661 ocean cruise passengers and 212 vessel calls, a 5.5-fold rise in passenger traffic and a 2.1-fold rise in vessel calls since 2013-14. The Cruise Bharat Mission, launched in September 2024, targets 1 million sea cruise passengers and 400,000 jobs by March 2029.
Twenty river cruise circuits across 16 National Waterways are already operating, and 51 more have been identified for development in phases. Sonowal said 143 river cruise terminals and landing points are operational. The two initiatives together are expected to generate more than 560,000 jobs and save 16 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions, Sonowal said.
Sonowal highlighted the development of National Waterway No. 5 in Odisha, estimated to cost more than Rs 13,000 crore. The waterway is meant to link the state's industrial and mining centers, including Talcher and Kalinganagar, with ports on the east coast.
Members of Parliament praised the government's efforts to develop the maritime sector and offered suggestions on maritime infrastructure in different parts of the country.
"I extend my deep gratitude to the MPs for their valuable insights and suggestions, which will help shape this journey,"
Sonowal
said. "Led by PM Modi's vision, we are steadily advancing towards a competitive, sustainable and thriving maritime ecosystem for a Viksit Bharat.”

Alongside showcasing handicrafts, handloom products and indigenous art forms, the 15-day Mela is emerging as a vibrant celebration of India's inclusive participation.
Organised around the theme
‘प्रकाश
और
परंपरा
–
ज्योति
से
ज्योति
जलाएँ
’
, the Mela celebrates India's traditional crafts, festive lighting and cultural heritage.
The Mela has been curated around seven thematic zones, each offering a distinctive experience showcasing India's crafts, traditions, food and cultural expressions. कला आँगन features live craft demonstrations; प्रकाश चौक showcases lamps and lights; पूजा पथ presents devotional products; सजावट बाज़ार focuses on home décor; घराना features textiles and fashion; स्वाद चौक offers food; and मंच hosts cultural activities and performances.
The Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022. Through 15 such fairs, more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.
After inauguration of the Mela on Monday evening, the Hon'ble Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, visited the stalls and interacted with stall managers and visitors, taking keen interest in the products and traditional crafts on display.
The Minister’s interaction with the participating artisans provided an opportunity to appreciate their creativity, skills and entrepreneurial efforts.
Dr Kumar’s visit also highlighted the importance of providing artisans from various communities with financial constraints, with platforms to showcase their products, connect with consumers and expand their livelihood opportunities.
A special attraction of the Mela is the series of cultural activities and programmes organised during the evening hours, where artists and performers from different States come together to present their respective art forms and cultural traditions.
The visitors are mesmerized with the cultural programmes wherein artists and performers present their colourful cultural presentations.
Through music, dance and other artistic performances, these programmes offer visitors an opportunity to experience the diverse cultural expressions of different regions of the country on one platform.
The evening programmes provide a common stage for artists from different parts of India to share their artistic heritage, celebrate regional identities and promote cultural exchange.
These performances add to the festive atmosphere of the Mela while highlighting the richness and diversity of India's traditional and contemporary cultural expressions.
The Mela brings together traditional craftsmanship, handloom products, live craft demonstrations and cultural performances, while promoting entrepreneurship, livelihood generation and inclusive participation.
The Mela features more than 130 stalls showcasing handicrafts, handloom products and creative works by artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities.
A key component of the Mela is Bharat TULIP, which seeks to connect artisans with wider markets through e-commerce platforms, enabling them to expand their reach and strengthen their economic opportunities. The initiative also contributes to preserving India's traditional arts and crafts by providing artisans with greater visibility and access to consumers.
Through Purple Fest, the Mela further celebrates the creativity, abilities and contributions of persons with disabilities, encouraging equal opportunities, participation and inclusion in society.
The participating beneficiaries are supported by the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) and National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC). They are being provided free stalls along with facilities such as travel expenses, daily allowance and transportation of goods to facilitate their participation.
Through this initiative, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues its efforts to strengthen livelihood opportunities, promote traditional craftsmanship, encourage entrepreneurship and foster inclusive economic growth while celebrating India's rich cultural heritage.
The Mela invites visitors to explore India's traditional crafts, support artisan communities and experience the country's vibrant cultural diversity through its art, craftsmanship, music and performances.
The Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 will remain open to visitors at Dilli Haat, INA, New Delhi, until November 15, 2026.

title: Union Minister Dr Virendra Kumar to Launch ‘Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan’, a National Intergenerational Bonding Campaign, Tomorrow in National Capital

Vayo SAATHI Volunteer Initiative To Mobilise Citizens Aged 18 Years And Above For The Welfare, Care And Social Inclusion Of Senior Citizens


Handbook Outlining The Campaign Framework And Implementation Roles Of States, Districts And Community Institutions To Be Released

date:

                03 NOV 2026 4:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, will launch the
‘Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan’ – National Intergenerational Bonding Campaign
under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), in National Capital here tomorrow.
Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, will formally launch the campaign, marking an important step towards strengthening intergenerational solidarity and promoting a society that values the experience, wisdom and contribution of senior citizens.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said the national campaign seeks to institutionalise meaningful and sustained engagement between senior citizens and younger generations, fostering mutual respect, understanding, companionship and shared responsibility.
He said the
Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan
is not merely a welfare campaign, but a nationwide social movement to institutionalise intergenerational solidarity, recognise senior citizens as contributors to society and mobilise youth participation in the cause of dignified ageing.
The Official added the Campaign envisages intergenerational bonding as a community-driven movement, encouraging families, educational institutions, youth organisations, voluntary organisations and local institutions to create opportunities for meaningful interaction and collaboration between generations.
The Ministry Official said the
Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan
seeks to respond to the emerging challenges by creating an enabling environment in which the younger generation can learn from the life experiences, knowledge, skills and cultural heritage of senior citizens, while older persons can benefit from the energy, technological awareness and contemporary perspectives of youth.
The initiative recognises senior citizens not merely as beneficiaries of welfare programmes but as active contributors, mentors and valuable repositories of knowledge, culture and social experience, he added.
The Official noted that India is undergoing a significant demographic transition, with the population of senior citizens steadily increasing adding the population aged 60 years and above is projected to grow from approximately 10 crore in 2011 to 23 crore by 2036, with its share in the total population rising from 8.4 per cent to 14.9 per cent.
Alongside this demographic shift, urbanisation, migration, changing family structures and evolving social patterns have, in many instances, reduced opportunities for regular interaction between generations, he said.
The Official said these developments underline the need for a structured and sustained approach to addressing social isolation, strengthening community support systems and ensuring that senior citizens remain active, respected and meaningfully connected with society.
He further said the Abhiyan is structured around an innovative
‘5C’ model – Connect, Converse, Co-create, Contribute and Continue
, which provides a practical framework for building meaningful relationships between generations and sustaining them through regular community participation.
The five components seek to
Connect by c
reating opportunities for senior citizens and younger generations to interact through community platforms, educational institutions and social initiatives,
Converse to e
ncourage dialogue, storytelling, exchange of experiences and mutual understanding between generations,
Co-create to f
acilitate joint activities, creative initiatives and collaborative projects drawing upon the complementary strengths of senior citizens and youth,
Contribute to e
nable both generations to contribute their knowledge, skills, time and capabilities towards community welfare and social development and
Continue to e
nsure that intergenerational engagement evolves into a regular, sustained and community-led practice rather than remaining limited to one-time activities.
The Official informed that the Campaign will be implemented across twelve thematic areas, offering diverse opportunities for participation and collaboration. These include
‘30 Minutes Together’
,
‘Teach Me – I'll Teach You’, ‘My Story, My India’, ‘Digital Dada-Dadi / Digital Saathi’, ‘Generation Health & Wellness’ and ‘Silver Skills – Seniors as Mentors’
,
among other activities.
He said through these themes, the Abhiyan will promote companionship, oral history and cultural exchange, digital literacy, health awareness, wellness, skill-sharing and mentorship.
It will also encourage young people to assist senior citizens in navigating digital services and identifying potential cyber fraud, thereby strengthening their confidence and safety in an increasingly technology-driven environment, he said.
The Official elaborated that a key component of the launch will be the introduction of
Vayo SAATHI – Support, Awareness, Assistance, Training, Health and Inclusion
, a digitally enabled volunteer initiative designed to mobilise citizens and institutions in support of the welfare, dignity and social inclusion of senior citizens.
He said the initiative seeks to develop a nationwide network of volunteers who can contribute their time, skills and resources to support older persons at the grassroots level. It is open to all citizens aged 18 years and above, including students, young professionals, community volunteers, civil society organisations and institutional partners, he further said.
Under the initiative, volunteers will be encouraged to serve as friends, facilitators, connectors and support persons for senior citizens, helping them access relevant information, welfare services, community activities, digital assistance and other forms of support, the Official said. He added that the framework will complement and strengthen existing institutional and community-based support systems.
The Ministry Official said the interested citizens can register as Vayo SAATHI volunteers through the
Senior Citizens Welfare (SCW) SAMAVESH Portal or the JEEVAN App
. Registered volunteers will also receive a Vayo SAATHI Certificate in recognition of their participation and contribution.
Through this initiative, the Ministry seeks to transform volunteerism into a structured, accessible and scalable mechanism for community participation in senior citizens' welfare, he added.
Union Minister is also scheduled to release a
Handbook on Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan
on the occasion. The Handbook will serve as a guiding document for the campaign, detailing its objectives, implementation framework, thematic activities and mechanisms for community participation.
It will also delineate the roles and responsibilities of States, Districts and community institutions, facilitating coordinated implementation and wider outreach across the country. The Handbook is intended to support the adoption of the campaign at different administrative and community levels and encourage active participation by educational institutions, youth groups, voluntary organisations and other stakeholders.
As part of the launch programme, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment will sign two Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with
Shri Ram Chandra Mission (SRCM)
and
Adhyatma Vigyan Satsang Kendra (AVSK), Jodhpur.
These partnerships aim to promote the holistic wellbeing of senior citizens through meditation, yoga and other wellness-oriented programmes. They will also support intergenerational engagement through community-based activities and sensitisation initiatives, including pledge drives and walkathons, encouraging greater public awareness and collective responsibility towards the welfare of older persons.
These collaborations reflect the Ministry’s commitment to engaging civil society organisations and other institutional partners in expanding the reach of senior citizens' welfare initiatives and promoting healthy, active and dignified ageing.
The Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan represents a broader effort to strengthen the social fabric through intergenerational solidarity and collective participation. By bringing senior citizens and youth together on common platforms, the campaign seeks to promote a culture in which experience and innovation complement each other, traditional wisdom is valued, and older persons remain integral to community life.
The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment invites citizens, educational institutions, universities, youth organisations, NGOs, resident welfare associations, community institutions and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) partners to actively participate in the campaign and register as Vayo SAATHI volunteers.
Through sustained public participation, institutional partnerships and community-led initiatives, the Abhiyan aspires to build a society in which senior citizens lead lives marked by dignity, respect, security, active participation and inclusion, while younger generations develop a deeper appreciation of their responsibilities towards older persons.
The campaign seeks to reinforce the principle that the welfare of senior citizens is not merely a governmental responsibility but a shared social commitment, requiring the active participation of every generation.
It is pertinent to mention that Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) is a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment aimed at promoting the welfare, care, protection and empowerment of senior citizens. Through its various interventions, the scheme seeks to facilitate an enabling environment for older persons to lead healthy, active, dignified and productive lives, with access to appropriate support services and opportunities for social participation.

His journey reflects the importance of timely intervention, professional rehabilitation, family support and sustained follow-up care in helping individuals overcome substance dependence and reintegrate into society.
The 40 year Ramesh Kumar, a resident of Pedhapalli district of Telangana, faced significant personal, family and professional challenges due to alcohol addiction. His alcohol consumption began during his early adult years, influenced by peer pressure and negative social influences, and gradually developed into addiction. Over time, this adversely affected his health, family relationships, behaviour and employment.
He experienced emotional distress, withdrew from social activities and struggled to maintain financial and professional stability. Despite these difficulties, he remained willing to seek treatment and rebuild his life, while his family continued to extend support throughout his journey towards recovery.
A significant turning point came through the intervention under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Through the Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA), operated by Prakriti Environment Society in Pedhapalli, Telangana, he received comprehensive de-addiction treatment and rehabilitation services.
The support included medical supervision, individual and family counselling, group therapy, motivational enhancement, relapse prevention therapy and regular follow-up sessions.
The rehabilitation programme helped him develop effective coping mechanisms, regain self-confidence and address the emotional and psychological challenges associated with addiction. He also received vocational guidance, medical intervention and support for social reintegration. Continuous counselling and family participation played an important role in strengthening his commitment to recovery and helping him maintain a healthier lifestyle.
The intervention has brought a positive transformation in his personal and professional life. Ramesh has successfully overcome alcohol dependence and is now sober and regularly employed.
His employment has become more stable, and he currently earns approximately Rs 12,000–15,000 per month. The improvement in his health, emotional well-being and financial stability has also contributed to better family circumstances.

He also highlighted the potential of recovering critical minerals from secondary resources such as coal fly ash, red mud, mine tailings and electronic waste, while underscoring the importance of translating research into commercially viable technologies and promoting sustainable resource utilisation.

The collaboration aims to strengthen indigenous capabilities, facilitate technology translation and promote stronger linkages among government, academia, research institutions and industry.

title: Launch of “India S&T Scoreboard” on 3rd November 2026 in New Delhi
date:

content:
NITI Aayog launched the “India S&T Scoreboard” on 3rd November 2026 at the Civil Services Officer’s Institute (CSOI), KG Marg, New Delhi. The Scoreboard was unveiled by
Shri
Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog. Developed as a key NITI Aayog initiative, the Scoreboard is an interactive platform that provides an integrated se se view of the science & technology landscape of Indian States and UTs. It has been designed to facilitate evidence-based policymaking and benchmarking across States/ UTs. Prof. Vivek Kumar Singh, Senior Adviser, NITI Aayog, welcomed the participants and set out the context and objectives of the exercise. He added that the Scoreboard has been built to go beyond the volume of output and capture quality, impact and collaboration, so that States can identify expertise and areas for focused action.
Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology noted that the Scoreboard adds a valuable State-level picture to the national evidence base on science and technology, and highlighted the role of State S&T Councils and State universities in widening India’s research base. Dr. T. Srinivasa Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences underscored that earth sciences are closely linked to every State, and that local capacity in science and technology is essential for States to make effective use of forecasts, early warnings and opportunities in the ocean sector.
Prof. Abhay Karandikar, Member (S&T), NITI Aayog emphasized that sound policy in science and technology must rest on reliable and comparable evidence. He observed that data on research and innovation has so far remained fragmented across multiple sources, making it difficult for States to assess where they stand. The Scoreboard addresses this gap by bringing ecosystem, publication and patent data together on a single interactive dashboard, with trends over years, so that States can track their progress over time.
Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog emphasized that India’s further progress in science and technology requires a more active role by the States. Guided by the principle of cooperative and competitive federalism, he noted that the Scoreboard will help States identify their strengths and gaps, learn from one another, and design better programmes and policies in science and technology. He urged all States and UTs to make full use of the platform.
The Scoreboard brings together data on the S&T ecosystem, including higher education institutions, R&D institutions, deep tech startups, and incubators, along with S&T outputs like research publications and patents. Going beyond the volume of output, it presents indicators of research quality, impact, collaboration and open access across priority research areas and three sectors, namely Academia, Government R&D Labs and Industry. It also enables side by side comparison of States/ UTs and provides detailed State profiles, including State policies and best practices.
The launch was followed by a walkthrough of the Scoreboard and a technical session on its methodology and data sources. Distinguished invitees from state government and academia shared their observations and suggestions for the further development of the platform. Representatives of states noted that the platform will support their planning, and help build institutional capacity and skilled human resources in science and technology at the state level. The deliberations reaffirmed that a reliable and comparable evidence base on science and technology at the State level will play an important role in strengthening State S&T ecosystems and in advancing India’s journey towards the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported sale and trafficking of girl children from border districts of Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan to cities in Maharashtra
subtitle:
​​​​​​​
Reportedly, parents sell their daughters to middlemen for Rs. 3 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh due to poverty and other reasons

The Commission issues notices to the Chief Secretaries and Directors General of Police of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Maharashtra, calling for detailed reports on the matter within two weeks
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 NOV 2026 5:36PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report that a large number of minor girl children are being sold for Rs. 3 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh by their parents to middlemen in several districts along the borders of Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. Subsequently, these small girls are trafficked by middlemen with the help of false documents showing them as their adopted children. On gaining adulthood, they are sold for Rs. 35 lakh to Rs. 40 lakh in different cities of Maharashtra for sex trade after changing their personal details to hide their identities.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of the human rights of the victim girl children. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Chief Secretaries and Directors General of Police of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Maharashtra, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.
According to the media report, carried on 30th October 2026, parents sell their girl child due to poverty and other reasons. The media report has quoted four specific cases of such trafficked girls.
